idiom_name: injected FeatureFlags struct built from ProcessInfo.environment; #if for build-time
implementation_notes: The router is a value type built once at launch: ProcessInfo.processInfo.environment["FF_NEW_CHECKOUT"] (or a plist entry, a remote-config payload or a UserDefaults value) is parsed into a FeatureFlags struct that is injected into the objects that need it, so the toggle point stays a boolean read and tests construct their own FeatureFlags without touching the environment. Build-time selection uses conditional compilation blocks (#if NEW_CHECKOUT) driven by Active Compilation Conditions or -D flags; because a conditionally compiled section must be syntactically complete, that form is for whole alternative implementations, not for fine-grained gating. A provider SDK becomes justified when flags must be targeted or administered outside the app.
pitfalls: Environment variables are supplied by the scheme, the launcher or the test runner, not by an App Store build: a production toggle needs a persisted or remote source instead of ProcessInfo.
Reading ProcessInfo inline at the toggle point hides the dependency and makes the branch untestable; inject the FeatureFlags value and let tests choose.
A #if block must be syntactically complete and is fixed per configuration, so using it for runtime intent ships a new binary per flag state.
A let-captured flag in a long-lived singleton never observes a change; re-read or pass a closure when the value must be refreshed.
